title: Bekhorot 30
description: Who is suspected of what: the Sabbatical Year, tithes and ritual purity, and then a run of baraitot on how an am ha’aretz becomes a trusted ḥaver, from washing his hands to accepting before three ḥaverim.
topics: 🥜 Rava bars a deceitful butcher even from selling nuts

a1.he: תַּרְבָּא דְּאַטְמָא בְּמַר דְּכַנְתָּא, קַנְסֵיהּ רָבָא לְזַבּוֹנֵי אֲפִילּוּ אַמְגּוֹזֵי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֲפִילּוּ מַיִם וָמֶלַח נָמֵי!

a2.he: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וּבְאִיסּוּרָא דְּגוּפֵיהּ קָנְסִינַן לֵיהּ. סְתָם דַּרְדְּקֵי גְּרוּ בְּאַמְגּוֹזֵי, וְאָזֵיל וּמְשַׁבֵּשׁ לִבְנֵי טַבָּחֵי, וְגָרֵי לְהוּ בְּאַמְגּוֹזֵי, וּמַיְיתוּ לֵיהּ תַּרְבָּא דְּאַטְמָא, וּמְזַבֵּין לֵיהּ בְּמַר דְּכַנְתָּא.

a3.he: מַתְנִי׳ הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית — אֵינוֹ חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת, הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת — אֵינוֹ חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית. הֶחָשׁוּד עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה — חָשׁוּד עַל הַטְּהָרוֹת, וְיֵשׁ שֶׁהוּא חָשׁוּד עַל הַטְּהָרוֹת — וְאֵינוֹ חָשׁוּד לֹא עַל זֶה וְלֹא עַל זֶה. זֶה הַכְּלָל: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל דָּבָר — לֹא דָּנוֹ וְלֹא מְעִידוֹ.

a4.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא? שְׁבִיעִית לָא בָּעֲיָא חוֹמָה, מַעֲשֵׂר — כֵּיוָן דְּבָעֵי חוֹמָה, חֲמִיר לֵיהּ.

a5.he: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר. מַאי טַעְמָא? מַעֲשֵׂר אִית לֵיהּ פִּדְיוֹן, שְׁבִיעִית — כֵּיוָן דְּקָא מִיתַּסְרָא לֵיהּ וְלֵית לֵיהּ פִּדְיוֹן — חֲמִירָא לֵיהּ.

a6.he: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה. כֵּיוָן דַּחֲשִׁיד אַדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַדְּרַבָּנַן.

a7.he: וְיֵשׁ חָשׁוּד עַל הַטְּהָרוֹת. מַאי טַעְמָא? נְהִי אַדְּרַבָּנַן חֲשִׁיד, אַדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא חֲשִׁיד. וּרְמִינְהִי: נֶאֱמָן עַל הַטְּהָרוֹת — נֶאֱמָן עַל שְׁבִיעִית, הָא חֲשִׁיד — חֲשִׁיד!

a8.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַי: מַתְנִיתִין כְּשֶׁרְאִינוּהוּ שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בְּצִינְעָא בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ.

a9.he: רַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דַּהֲוָה חֲשִׁיד לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ, וַאֲתָא קַמֵּי רַבָּנַן וְקַבֵּיל אַתַּרְוַיְיהוּ, וַהֲדַר אִיחֲשַׁד אַחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ, דְּאָמְרִינַן: מִיגּוֹ דַּחֲשִׁיד אַהָא — חֲשִׁיד נָמֵי אַאִידַּךְ.

a10.he: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְתִימְתָּאָה, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית — חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.

a11.he: מַאן חֲכָמִים? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דִּבְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שְׁבִיעִית חֲמִירָא לְהוּ, דְּהָהוּא דַּהֲוָה קָרֵי לֵיהּ לְחַבְרֵיהּ ״דַּיָּירָא בַּר דַּיָּירְתָּא״, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תֵּיתֵי לִי דְּלָא אֲכַלִי פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית כְּוָותָךְ.

a12.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְתִימְתָּאָה, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית. וּמַאן חֲכָמִים? רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: חָשׁוּד לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי חָשׁוּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ.

a13.he: רַבִּי יוֹנָה וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה תַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי זְעֵירָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹנָה וְרַבִּי זְעֵירָא תַּלְמִידֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, חַד אָמַר: אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית

b1.he: חָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר, וּמַאן חֲכָמִים? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְחַד אָמַר: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית, וּמַאן חֲכָמִים? רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

b2.he: דְּתַנְיָא: עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת, וְנֶחְשַׁד לְדָבָר אֶחָד — נֶחְשַׁד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ נֶחְשָׁד אֶלָּא לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר בִּלְבַד.

b3.he: הַגֵּר שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, אֲפִילּוּ נֶחְשַׁד לְדָבָר אֶחָד — הָוֵי חָשׁוּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ, וַהֲרֵי הוּא כְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּמָּד. נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ, דְּאִי קַדֵּישׁ — קִידּוּשָׁיו קִידּוּשִׁין.

b4.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת, חוּץ מִדָּבָר אֶחָד — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ. גּוֹי שֶׁבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, חוּץ מִדָּבָר אֶחָד — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ דִּקְדּוּק אֶחָד מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים.

b5.he: וְכֵן בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי לְוִיָּה, וְכֹהֵן שֶׁבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי כְהוּנָּה, חוּץ מִדָּבָר אֶחָד — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַמַּקְרִיב אֶת דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים וְגוֹ׳״, הָעֲבוֹדָה הַמְּסוּרָה לִבְנֵי אַהֲרֹן, כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָּהּ — אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּכְּהוּנָּה.

b6.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת, אִם רְאִינוּהוּ שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בְּצִינְעָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ — מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ. וְאִם לָאו — מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ, וְהוּא לָמֵד כְּדַרְכּוֹ וְהוֹלֵךְ.

b7.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְקַבְּלִין לִכְנָפַיִם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין לִטְהָרוֹת, וְאִם אָמַר: ״אֵינִי מְקַבֵּל אֶלָּא לִכְנָפַיִם״ — מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ. קִיבֵּל לַטְּהָרוֹת וְלֹא קִיבֵּל לַכְּנָפַיִם — אַף לַטְּהָרוֹת לֹא קִיבֵּל.

b8.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד כַּמָּה מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ? בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: לְמַשְׁקִין — שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, לִכְסוּת — שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ.

b9.he: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל, אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה לִשְׁלשִׁים.

b10.he: (סִימָן: חָבֵר, תַּלְמִיד, תְּכֵלֶת, מֶכֶס, חָזַר, גַּבַּאי, בְּעַצְמוֹ).

b11.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת — צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, וּבָנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה חָבֵר שֶׁקִּיבֵּל לְבֶן חָבֵר שֶׁקִּיבֵּל.

b12.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת — צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, וַאֲפִילּוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים. זָקֵן וְיוֹשֵׁב בִּישִׁיבָה — אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, שֶׁכְּבָר קִיבֵּל עָלָיו מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁיָּשַׁב. אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁאֲחֵרִים מְקַבְּלִין לְפָנָיו.

b13.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיסְתַּפַּק לְהוּ מִילְּתָא בִּטְהָרוֹת, שַׁדַּרוּ רַבָּנַן לְגַבֵּי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס, אֵזִילוּ אֱמַרוּ לֵיהּ: לְעַיֵּין בַּהּ. אַשְׁכְּחוּהּ דְּקָא טָעֵין טְהָרוֹת, אוֹתֵיב רַבָּנַן מִדִּידֵיהּ לְגַבַּיְיהוּ, וְקָאֵי אִיהוּ לְעַיּוֹנֵי בַּהּ.

b14.he: אֲתוֹ אָמְרִי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אָבִיו שֶׁל זֶה בִּיזָּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, אַף הוּא מְבַזֶּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים!

b15.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כְּבוֹד זָקֵן יְהֵא מוּנָּח בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, אֶלָּא מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נָהֲגוּ כֹּהֲנִים סִילְסוּל בְּעַצְמָן, שֶׁאֵין מוֹסְרִין אֶת הַטְּהָרוֹת לְכׇל אָדָם.

b16.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָבֵר שֶׁמֵּת — אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ הֲרֵי הֵן בְּחֶזְקָתָן, עַד שֶׁיֵּחָשֵׁדוּ. וְכֵן חָצֵר שֶׁמּוֹכְרִין בָּהּ תְּכֵלֶת — הֲרֵי הִיא בְּחֶזְקָתָהּ, עַד שֶׁתִּיפָּסֵל.

b17.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר, וְכֵן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר, וְכֵן עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לְחָבֵר — כּוּלָּן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת בַּתְּחִלָּה. אֲבָל אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ, וְכֵן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ, וְכֵן עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ — אֵין צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת בַּתְּחִלָּה.

b18.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הֵן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל עֲלֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת לְכַתְּחִלָּה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה אַחַת שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר וְהָיְתָה קוֹמַעַת לוֹ תְּפִילִּין עַל יָדוֹ, נִשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ וְהָיְתָה קוֹשֶׁרֶת לוֹ קִשְׁרֵי מוֹכֵס עַל יָדוֹ.

messages.text: Continued from 29b: the mishna ruled that from one suspected of selling teruma as non-sacred produce, Rabbi Yehuda says one may not buy even water and salt, while Rabbi Shimon says one may not buy anything that has relevance to teruma and tithes. The Gemara then told of a certain butcher who was suspected of selling…
Gemara
…fat of the kidney adjacent to the thigh, which is forbidden, in place of fat of the intestines, which is permitted. Rava penalized him and prohibited him even from selling nuts.
messages.lead: There was a certain butcher who was suspected of selling

notes.he: חלב הכליות שעל הירך:
notes.en: Tarba de’atma: the fat of the kidneys that lies on the thigh.

notes.he: בחזקת חלב טהור הנקרא כנתא ובלע"ז אנטריי"ל כמו הדרא דכנתא דאמרינן בשחיטת חולין (דף מח:):
notes.en: Bemar dekhanta: [he sold it] as though it were permitted fat, which is called kanta (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), as in “the hadra dekhanta” that we mention in Shechitat Chullin (48b).

notes.he: כך גריס רבינו תם פירוש מר בחילוף של כנתא כמו במר דשחוטה דבפרק גיד הנשה (חולין צד.) וכמו במר דפרזלא דבבא קמא (דף קיג:):
notes.en: Tarba de’atma bemar dekhanta: this is how Rabbeinu Tam reads it. Mar means “in exchange for” kanta, as in “bemar deshechuta” in chapter Gid HaNasheh (Chullin 94a), and as in “bemar defarzela” in Bava Kamma (113b).

notes.he: והיה אחד שהוא טהור של הדורא דכנתא דכנתא טהור כמו דכי ואמר לן רבי דאמר משמיה דרבי יצחק האורליני ז"ל דהוא אמר דאקשתא ואייתרא דקאמר בשחיטת חולין בחלב של קיבה הוו אבל הדורא דכנתא כוליה טהור:
notes.en: Who would sell fat bemadkhanta: [a printed correction reads: he would sell fat of the thigh and say that it was permitted (“pure”); so it should read, and so it is in the Arukh, entry markanta.] [He passed it off as fat] that is permitted, of the hadura dekhanta; kanta means permitted, like “clean.” Our teacher told us, saying in the name of Rabbi Yitzḥak HaOrlini, that the akashta and the aitra mentioned in Shechitat Chullin are fats of the abomasum, but the hadura dekhanta is entirely permitted.

messages.text: @Rava In accordance with which opinion in the mishna is your ruling? It must be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda. If it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, then you should prohibit this butcher from selling even water and salt.
messages.quote: Rava penalized him and prohibited him even from selling nuts

notes.he: דקניס הכל:
notes.en: In accordance with whom? Rabbi Yehuda: who penalizes everything.

notes.dh: אי הכי אפילו מים ומלח נמי
notes.he: ליקנסיה מ"ט לא קנסיה אלא אמגוזי:
notes.en: If so, even water and salt too: he should penalize him for them. Why did he penalize him only for nuts?

messages.text: Actually, my ruling is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, who holds that one is suspected only about those items that are related to the prohibition in question. And we are in fact penalizing him with regard to items related to the prohibition itself.
messages.quote: It must be in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda

notes.he: דלא קניס אלא במידי דדמי לאיסורא ובאיסורא גופיה במידי דעביד איסורא דהיינו אמגוזי:
notes.en: Actually, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon: who penalizes only for something similar to the prohibition. And here it is the prohibition itself, for the thing with which he commits the prohibition, namely the nuts.

notes.he: דאמר כל שיש בו זיקה והאי נמי אמגוזי זיקה דאיסורא נינהו:
notes.en: Actually, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon: who says, anything that has a connection [to the prohibition]; and these nuts too are connected to the prohibition.

messages.text: How so? Ordinary children are enticed by nuts, and that individual went and misled the children of butchers and enticed them with nuts, and they brought him fat of the kidney that is adjacent to the thigh, and he sold it as though it were fat of the intestines.

notes.he: גרורים ומשוכים אחר אגוזים:
notes.en: Geru be’amguzei: are drawn and pulled after nuts.

notes.he: מטעה אותם באגוזים ושוכרן לבני הטבחים ומביאין לו החלב שגונבין אותו מאביהן והוא מוכרו במר דכנתא:
notes.en: And misleads the butchers’ children: he leads them astray with nuts and hires the butchers’ children with them, and they bring him the fat, which they steal from their fathers, and he sells it as permitted fat.

notes.he: מימשכי:
notes.en: Geru: are drawn.

messages.text: Mishna
One who is suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year is not suspect with regard to tithes;

notes.he: ולוקחין ממנו תבואה בשאר שני שבוע ואין צריכים לעשר ודאי אלא דמאי. וטעמא דכולה מתני' מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Mishna. Is not suspect with regard to tithes: so one may buy produce from him in the other years of the seven-year cycle, and need not tithe it as certainly untithed, only as demai. The reason for the whole mishna is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: למכרו דאסור למכור שביעית:
notes.en: One who is suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year: of selling it, for it is forbidden to sell [produce of] the Sabbatical Year.

messages.text: and likewise, one who is suspect with regard to tithes is not suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year.
One who is suspect with regard to this, the Sabbatical Year, or with regard to that, tithes, is suspect with regard to selling ritually impure foods as though they were ritually pure items.
But there are those who are suspect with regard to ritually pure items who are not suspect with regard to this, the Sabbatical Year, nor with regard to that, tithes.
This is the principle with regard to these matters: Anyone who is suspect with regard to a specific matter may neither adjudicate cases nor testify in cases involving that matter.
Gemara

What is the reason? One is not required to eat produce of the Sabbatical Year within the wall of Jerusalem, and therefore he treats it lightly. As for second tithe, since one is required to eat it only within the wall of Jerusalem, it is possible that it seems more stringent for him, and therefore he is not suspect, despite the suspicions with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year.
messages.quote: One who is suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year is not suspect with regard to tithes

notes.he: דאינו יכול לאכול מעשר שני אלא לפנים מחומת ירושלים דכתיב (דברים י״ד:כ״ג) ואכלת לפני ה' אלהיך וגו':
notes.en: Gemara. Requires a wall: for one may eat second tithe only inside the wall of Jerusalem, as it is written: “And you shall eat before the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 14:23).

notes.he: מכאן מדקדק רבינו תם בכ"מ שהזכיר מעשר אצל שביעית דמיירי בנותן מעשר שני לשם חולין כגון הרי אלו בחזקתן למעשר ולשביעית בפרק הנזקין (גיטין סא:) וכן אינו חושש לתבלין שבה לא משום שביעית ולא משום מעשר בפ"ק דחולין (דף ו.) ולשון מעשר נמי מוכיח כן דהיכא דאיירי בחששא דאינו מתוקן נקיט טבל או דמאי:
notes.en: Tithes, which require a wall, are stringent for him: from here Rabbeinu Tam infers that wherever tithe is mentioned alongside the Sabbatical Year, it speaks of one who treats second tithe as non-sacred. For example: “These remain in their presumptive status with regard to tithes and the Sabbatical Year,” in chapter HaNizakin (Gittin 61b); and likewise, “he need not be concerned about the spices in it, neither due to the Sabbatical Year nor due to tithe,” in the first chapter of Chullin (6a). The word “tithe” also proves it, for where the concern is that the produce has not been tithed, the Talmud says tevel or demai.

messages.text: What is the reason? Since there is redemption for tithes, one might treat them lightly. As for produce of the Sabbatical Year, since it is always prohibited to him and there is no redemption of it, it is possible that it seems more stringent for him, and therefore he is not suspect.
messages.lead: The mishna teaches: One who is suspect with regard to tithe is not suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: כיון דמיתסרא ליה לסחורה ולית ליה פדיון כדאמרי' האחרון נתפס בשביעית ופירי עצמו אסור:
notes.en: Since it is prohibited to him for trade and has no redemption: as we say, the last [item it is exchanged for] is caught up in the Sabbatical Year, and the produce itself remains prohibited.

messages.text: Since he is suspect with regard to matters that apply by Torah law, all the more so that he is suspect with regard to matters that are by rabbinic law. Eating non-sacred food in a state of ritual purity is an ordinance of the Sages; it does not apply by Torah law. Consequently, he is certainly not trusted with regard to that matter.
messages.quote: One who is suspect with regard to this, the Sabbatical Year, or with regard to that, tithes

notes.he: היינו שביעית ומעשר כ"ש אדרבנן:
notes.en: Since he is suspect regarding Torah law: that is, the Sabbatical Year and tithe; all the more so regarding rabbinic law.

messages.text: What is the reason? Granted, he is suspect with regard to prohibitions that are by rabbinic law, but he is not suspect with regard to prohibitions that are by Torah law.
messages.quote: But there are those who are suspect with regard to ritually pure items

notes.he: דרבנן נינהו שיהא אדם אוכל חולין בטהרה:
notes.en: The ritually pure items: they are rabbinic, that a person should eat non-sacred food in purity.

notes.he: דטהרות אוכלי חולין בטהרה אינו אלא מדרבנן:
notes.en: For [with] ritually pure items, eating non-sacred food in purity is only by rabbinic law.

messages.text: If one is trusted with regard to ritually pure items he is trusted with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year.
messages.lead: And the Gemara raises a contradiction from a baraita:

messages.text: It can be inferred from here that if he is suspect with regard to ritually pure items he is likewise suspect with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year.
messages.quote: trusted with regard to ritually pure items

notes.he: על הטהרות חשוד על השביעית:
notes.en: But one who is suspect: on ritually pure items is suspect on the Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: דמשמע ליה דלגופה לא איצטריך דפשיטא דכי נאמן על הטהרות דנאמן על השביעית כיון דנוהג מנהג פרושים שאוכל חולין בטהרה:
notes.en: But one who is suspect is suspect: [the Gemara draws this inference] because it holds that the statement itself was not needed, since it is obvious that one trusted on ritually pure items is trusted on the Sabbatical Year, as he conducts himself in the manner of the Perushim, who eat non-sacred food in purity.

notes.he: חשוד על הטהרות חשוד נמי אשביעית וקשיא למתני' דתני ויש שהוא חשוד על הטהרות ואינו חשוד לא על זה ועל זה:
notes.en: But: one who is suspect on ritually pure items is also suspect on the Sabbatical Year. And this is difficult for the mishna, which teaches: There are those suspect on ritually pure items who are suspect neither on this nor on that.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where they saw him practicing stringencies with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year and tithes privately, within his home. Since he himself is known to be trustworthy in these matters in private, he is not suspected of violating these prohibitions in his business, despite his lack of trustworthiness with regard to ritual purity.

notes.he: דקתני אין חשוד כגון שראינוהו שנוהג דין מעשרות ושביעית בצינעא בתוך ביתו דליכא למימר לפנים הוא עושה כיון דבצינעא קא עביד:
notes.en: The mishna: which teaches “is not suspect,” is where we saw him observing the law of tithes and the Sabbatical Year privately within his home. One cannot say he is doing it for show, since he does it privately.

notes.dh: מתני' כשראינוהו נוהג בצנעא בתוך ביתו
notes.he: שנזהר מן השביעית משמע דעם הארץ סתמא חשוד אשביעית כמו אטהרות ותימה דבסוף הניזקין (גיטין סא.) קאמר מאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא דמיקל באשת עם הארץ ומחמיר על החשודה על השביעית וקאמר רבא הכא במאי עסקינן בעם הארץ דרבי מאיר וטומאה וטהרה דרבנן ומדקתני גבי טומאה וטהרה עם הארץ סתם וגבי שביעית קתני החשודה משמע דסתם עמי הארץ חשידי אטהרות ולא חשידי אשביעית ומיהו מהא דשרי לבור ולטחון גבי עם הארץ דחשיד אטומאה וטהרה ולא אסרינן מטעם שביעית אין לדקדק כלום דדלמא בשאר שני שבוע איירי ההיא ולא בשביעית או בפירות הידועים שאינם של שביעית דה"נ איירי בפירות הידועים שהם מתוקנים לרבא דלית ליה שינוייא דאביי דרוב עמי הארץ מעשרין ועוד קשיא מכאן לפירוש ר"ת דמפרש בפ"ב דכתובות (דף כד.) גבי שלי חדש ושל חברי ישן דסתם עם הארץ אע"ג דחשידי אדמאי לא חשידי אשביעית וסותר פירוש רבינו שמואל דמפרש דחדש וישן דנקט משום שביעית וכי משני התם רוב עמי הארץ מעשרין רוצה לומר דהוא הדין בשביעית וכמה קושיות דמקשה רבינו תם על פי' רבינו שמואל כמו שפירש בכתובות ומפרש חדש וישן להשביח המקח בעלמא קאמר ולא לענין איסור והיתר והשתא לר' אילעא דחשוד אטהרות דרבנן חשוד אשביעית כל שכן סתם עמי הארץ דכי היכי דחשידי אדמאי דאורייתא חשידי נמי אשביעית ודוחק להעמיד סתם עם הארץ בכ"מ דלא חשיד אשביעית כשראינוהו נוהג בצינעא בתוך ביתו ועוד קשיא מהא דתנן במס' דמאי (פ"ג מ"ד) ומייתינן לה נמי בהניזקין (גיטין סא:) המוליך חטין לטוחן כותי או לטוחן ע"ה אינו חושש לא משום מעשר ולא משום שביעית משמע דסתם עמי הארץ חשידי אשביעית וי"ל משום כותי נקט שביעית אי נמי בודאי חשוד איירי וכן ההיא דהלוקח לולב מחבירו בשביעית דקאמר עלה בפ' לולב הגזול (סוכה לט.) דאין מוסרין דמי פירות שביעית לעם הארץ וכן הא דמייתי פרק קמא דחולין (דף ו.) הנותן לשכנתו עיסה לאפות וקדירה לבשל אינו חושש לשאור ולתבלין שבה לא משום שביעית ולא משום מעשר ואם אמר עשה לי משליכי חושש כו' כל הני מיירי בודאי חשוד וא"ת היכי מוכח מינה בחולין דגזרו על תערובות דמאי דלמא חשוד גרע מסתם עם הארץ לגבי מעשר ראשון כדמוכח בשילהי הנזקין (גיטין סא.) לאביי וי"ל דלרבא פריך שפיר דלא חמיר ליה:
notes.en: In brief: The mishna is where we saw him observing [the Sabbatical Year] privately within his home. This implies that an ordinary am ha’aretz is suspect on the Sabbatical Year just as on ritual purity. Tosafot find this difficult from the end of HaNizakin (Gittin 61a): asked why the mishna there is lenient with the wife of an am ha’aretz but strict with a woman suspected about the Sabbatical Year, Rava answers that it speaks of Rabbi Meir’s am ha’aretz and of rabbinic impurity; since it says simply “am ha’aretz” about purity but “one suspected” about the Sabbatical Year, ordinary amei ha’aretz are suspect on purity but not on the Sabbatical Year. (The ruling there permitting sifting and grinding with an am ha’aretz suspect on impurity proves nothing, since it may speak of the other years of the cycle, or of produce known not to be Sabbatical, just as, according to Rava, who rejects Abaye’s answer that most amei ha’aretz tithe, it speaks of produce known to be tithed.) It is also difficult for Rabbeinu Tam’s explanation in Ketubot (24a), at “mine is new and my fellow’s is old,” that an ordinary am ha’aretz, though suspect on demai, is not suspect on the Sabbatical Year. [Rabbeinu Tam there] rejects Rabbeinu Shmuel, who explains “new and old” with reference to the Sabbatical Year and reads the answer “most amei ha’aretz tithe” as applying to the Sabbatical Year too, and he explains “new and old” as mere praise of the goods, not a matter of prohibition. Now, according to Rabbi Ilai, one suspect on rabbinic purity is suspect on the Sabbatical Year; all the more so ordinary amei ha’aretz, who, just as they are suspect on demai, which is Torah law, are suspect on the Sabbatical Year. And it is forced to explain every ordinary am ha’aretz who is not suspect on the Sabbatical Year as one seen observing it privately in his home. A further difficulty: the mishna in Demai (3:4), cited in HaNizakin (Gittin 61b), says one who brings wheat to a Samaritan miller or an am ha’aretz miller need not be concerned for tithe or the Sabbatical Year, implying that ordinary amei ha’aretz are suspect on the Sabbatical Year. Answer: the Sabbatical Year is mentioned there because of the Samaritan, or else it speaks of one who is certainly suspect. So too the case of buying a lulav from one’s fellow in the Sabbatical Year, where we say one does not hand Sabbatical-Year money to an am ha’aretz (Sukka 39a), and the case of giving one’s neighbor dough to bake or a pot to cook, where one need not be concerned for the leaven and spices in it on account of the Sabbatical Year or tithe (Chullin 6a): all of these speak of one who is certainly suspect. And if you ask how the Gemara in Chullin proves from that case that the Sages decreed on mixtures of demai, since perhaps one who is suspect is worse than an ordinary am ha’aretz regarding first tithe, as is evident at the end of HaNizakin (Gittin 61a) according to Abaye: one can say that according to Rava the challenge stands, for he does not treat it as more stringent. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: חומרא דשביעית ומעשר בתוך ביתו:
notes.en: When we saw him observing: the stringency of the Sabbatical Year and tithe within his home.

messages.text: There is an alternative answer: The baraita is referring to a case where one was suspect with regard to both ritually pure items and produce of the Sabbatical Year, and he came before the Sages and accepted upon himself that he would observe both of them, and afterward he was suspected with regard to one of them.

notes.he: ברייתא דדייקינן מינה הא חשוד כגון דהוה חשוד אתרוייהו אשביעית ואטהרות וקביל אתרוייהו שיזהר על שניהם:
notes.en: Rabbi Yannai said: the baraita from which we inferred “but one who is suspect [is suspect]” is where he had been suspect on both, the Sabbatical Year and ritually pure items, and he accepted on both that he would be careful about both of them.

notes.he: לעולם כדאמר מתני' ומ"ט דברייתא דדייקא הא חשוד חשוד:
notes.en: Rabbi Yannai said: actually, it is as the mishna says. And what is the reason of the baraita, from which it is inferred “but one who is suspect is suspect”?

messages.text: The reason for the halakha here is that we say: Since he is suspect with regard to this one of them, he is also suspect with regard to the other one. Although one of the prohibitions is more stringent than the other, the court has seen that he cannot be trusted to keep his word about either of them.

notes.he: אטהרות ואשביעית ואמעשר ואתא לקמי רבנן וקיבל אתרוייהו ושוב איחשד אחדא ומש"ה כיון דתחלה היה חשוד אכולן ועכשיו חוזר להיות חשוד אחדא אמרינן נמי חשוד אכולן:
notes.en: For example, where he was suspect on both: on ritually pure items and on the Sabbatical Year and on tithe, and he came before the Rabbis and accepted on both, and then he was again suspected on one. Therefore, since at first he was suspect on all of them and now he is again suspect on one, we say that he is suspect on all of them as well.

messages.caption: The mishna’s four rules on who is suspect of what, with the Gemara’s reason for each.

messages.text: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed. Most unattributed statements of tanna’im were formulated by Rabbi Akiva’s students and reflect his opinions. But the Rabbis say: One who is suspect with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year is suspect with regard to tithe.
messages.quote: One who is suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year is not suspect with regard to tithes

notes.he: דחשוד על השביעית אינו חשוד על המעשר:
notes.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva: that one suspect on the Sabbatical Year is not suspect on tithe.

notes.he: זו דברי ר"ע סתימתאה הא סתמא דמתני' דתני חשוד על השביעית אינו חשוד על המעשרות ר"ע היא:
notes.en: This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed: this anonymous mishna, which teaches “one suspect on the Sabbatical Year is not suspect on tithes,” is Rabbi Akiva.

messages.text: Who are the Sages referred to here as the Rabbis? It is Rabbi Yehuda, as in Rabbi Yehuda’s locale they considered produce of the Sabbatical Year an especially stringent prohibition. Therefore, if a resident of that place was suspect with regard to the Sabbatical Year, he was certainly not trusted with regard to tithes.

notes.he: וכיון דחשוד אשביעית כ"ש אמעשרות:
notes.en: The Sabbatical Year is stringent for them: and since he is suspect on the Sabbatical Year, all the more so on tithes.

notes.dh: באתריה דרבי יהודה חמירא להו שביעית
notes.he: ולכך חשוד אמעשר ותימה דהא בפ"ק דשבת (דף יז:) אמרינן דבתרומה כיון דאפשר למיעבד כדשמואל דחטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי לא חשידי והכי נמי גבי מעשר שני לא הוה לן למיחשדיה כיון דאפשר למעבד כדשמואל דהקדש שוה מנה שחללו על שוה פרוטה מחולל דהוא הדין מעשר שני ובשאלתות דרב אחאי הוא בהדיא על כרם רבעי שמחללין אותו על דבר מועט ומעשר שני ונטע רבעי דין אחד להם בכ"מ דקדש קדש גמרינן להו מהדדי כדאיתא בפרק שני דקדושין (דף נד:) ואפי' לכתחלה מסתבר דשרי כמו גבי הקדש במסכת ערכין (דף כט.) דשרי בזמן הזה גבי ההוא גברא דאחרימינהו לנכסיה והא דמוקי בפרק התקבל (גיטין דף סה.) ההיא דכיצד מערימין על מעשר שני במעשר בזמן הזה דרבנן היה יכול להקשות בזמן הזה מאי הערמה צריך לפטור מחומש והלא יכול לחלל לשוה מנה על שוה פרוטה אלא מסלק ליה בפירכא אחריתי ואמה העבריה בזמן הזה מי איכא וכן מעשים בכל יום שאנו מחללין כרם רבעי שוה מנה על שוה פרוטה וי"ל דלא דמי מעשר לתרומה דפעמים שאין לו פרוטה מזומנת לחלל עליה וגם אין לו כי אם מעט מעשר כנגד שוה פרוטה ואינו רוצה ליתן פרוטה כנגדו:
notes.en: In brief: In Rabbi Yehuda’s locale the Sabbatical Year was stringent for them, and therefore [one suspect on it] is suspect on tithe. Tosafot ask: in the first chapter of Shabbat (17b) we say that with teruma, since one can do as Shmuel says, that a single grain of wheat exempts the whole pile, people are not suspected [of neglecting it]. So too with second tithe we should not suspect him, since one can do as Shmuel says, that consecrated property worth a maneh that was redeemed on a peruta’s worth is redeemed, and the same holds for second tithe. [Tosafot support this:] the She’iltot of Rav Aḥai states it explicitly of a fourth-year vineyard, that one redeems it on something small, and second tithe and fourth-year produce share one law everywhere, as they are derived from each other through “holy, holy” (Kiddushin 54b); and it seems permitted even ab initio, as with consecrated property in Arakhin (29a), where it is permitted nowadays, in the case of the man who devoted all his property. And when Gittin (65a) sets “how does one act cunningly with second tithe” in second tithe nowadays, which is rabbinic, it could have asked: nowadays, why is a stratagem needed to avoid the added fifth, when one can redeem a maneh’s worth on a peruta’s worth? Instead it rejects that with another objection: is there a Hebrew maidservant nowadays? And every day we redeem a fourth-year vineyard worth a maneh on a peruta’s worth. Tosafot answer that tithe is not comparable to teruma: sometimes one has no peruta at hand to redeem it on, or has only a little tithe, worth about a peruta, and does not want to give a peruta for it. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: ומדחשיד על החמור חשיד נמי אקל:
notes.en: And in Rabbi Yehuda’s locale the Sabbatical Year was stringent: and since he is suspect on the stringent one, he is also suspect on the lenient one.

messages.text: As in that locale, if a certain person would call another: A convert, son of a female convert, wishing to insult him, that person would say to him in reply: I have a blessing coming to me, as I do not eat produce of the Sabbatical Year like you do. This indicates that the accusation of eating produce of the Sabbatical Year was a great insult, since they treated the Sabbatical Year stringently.

notes.he: באתריה דרבי יהודה:
notes.en: For a certain person who would call his fellow: in Rabbi Yehuda’s locale.

notes.he: גר בן גיורת:
notes.en: Dayyara bar dayyarta: a convert, son of a female convert.

notes.he: שכר טוב שלא אכלתי פירות שביעית כוותך. יש מפרשים רבי עקיבא סתימתאה דאמרינן בסנהדרין באלו הן הנחנקין (סנהדרין דף פו.) סתם משנה רבי מאיר סתם ברייתא רבי נתן וכולהו אליבא דרבי עקיבא ולאו מילתא היא דהא בכמה דוכתין אמרינן רבי מנחם סתימתאה רבי שמעון סתימתאה אלא רוב משניות איכא בהש"ס סתומות אליבא דר' עקיבא:
notes.en: Teitei li: may a good reward come to me, for I did not eat Sabbatical-Year produce like you. Some explain “Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed” by what we say in Sanhedrin, chapter Elu Hen HaNeḥenakin (86a): an anonymous mishna is Rabbi Meir, an anonymous baraita is Rabbi Natan [so Rashi’s text here], and all of them follow Rabbi Akiva. But that is not right, for in several places we say “Rabbi Menaḥem, the unattributed,” “Rabbi Shimon, the unattributed.” Rather, [it means that] many mishnayot in the Talmud are anonymous in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: גר בת גיורת:
notes.en: Dayyora bat dayyorta: a convert, daughter of a female convert. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads “daughter of”; the daf reads “son of.”]

messages.text: There are those who say it was stated like this:
This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva, the unattributed. But the Rabbis say: One who is suspect with regard to tithe is suspect with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year.
And who are the Sages referred to here as the Rabbis? It is Rabbi Meir, who says: One who is suspect with regard to one matter is suspect with regard to the entire Torah.
Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Yirmeya, who were students of Rabbi Zeira, disagreed about this matter. And some say that it was Rabbi Yona and Rabbi Zeira, students of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who disagreed.
But the Rabbis say that one who is suspect with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year…

…is suspect with regard to tithe. And who are the Sages referred to here as the Rabbis? It is Rabbi Yehuda, as in his locale they treated the prohibition of produce of the Sabbatical Year stringently.
One who is suspect with regard to tithe is suspect with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year. And who are the Sages referred to here as the Rabbis? It is Rabbi Meir.

notes.dh: חשוד על המעשר חשוד על השביעית
notes.he: וכ"ש חשוד אשביעית חשוד אמעשר:
notes.en: One suspect on tithe is suspect on the Sabbatical Year: and all the more so, one suspect on the Sabbatical Year is suspect on tithe.

notes.he: דאמר לקמן חשוד לדבר אחד חשוד לכל התורה:
notes.en: And who are the Sages? Rabbi Meir: who says below that one suspect on one matter is suspect on the entire Torah.

messages.text: With regard to an am ha’aretz, i.e., one who is unreliable with regard to ritual impurity and tithes, who accepts upon himself the commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status, i.e., that he will be stringent in all matters observed by ḥaverim, including teruma, tithes, and ḥalla, and also undertake to eat only food that is ritually pure, and the Sages accepted him as trustworthy but subsequently he was suspected with regard to one matter in which others saw him act improperly, he is suspected with regard to the entire Torah. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say: He is suspected only with regard to that particular matter.

notes.dh: וחכמים אומרים אינו נחשד אלא על אותו דבר בלבד
notes.he: לר' אילעאי דלעיל דחשוד על הטהרות חשוד על השביעית אלא היכא שראינוהו נוהג בצינעא הא דקאמר הכא אינו נאסר אלא לאותו דבר לאו דוקא אלא לאותו דבר וכיוצא בו ולא אתא אלא לאפוקי בכל התורה כולה:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: He is suspected only with regard to that matter: according to Rabbi Ilai above, one suspect on ritually pure items is suspect on the Sabbatical Year, except where we saw him observing it privately. So what is said here, “he is suspected only with regard to that matter,” is not exact; it means that matter and what is like it, and it comes only to exclude the entire Torah.

messages.text: With regard to a convert who accepted upon himself upon his conversion matters of Torah, i.e., all of the mitzvot, even if he is suspect with regard to one matter alone, he is suspect with regard to the entire Torah, and he is considered like a Jewish transgressor [meshummad], who habitually transgresses the mitzvot.
messages.lead: It is also taught in a baraita:

notes.he: ולא אמרינן דליהוי עובד כוכבים גמור כאילו לא נתגייר:
notes.en: He is like a Jewish meshummad: and we do not say that he is a complete gentile, as though he had never converted.

messages.text: The practical difference resulting from the fact that he is considered like a Jewish transgressor is that if he betroths a woman, his betrothal is a valid betrothal, and they are married. Although he is suspect with regard to the entire Torah, he does not return to his prior gentile status.

notes.he: אשה לאחר שהמיר דתו קידושיו קידושין:
notes.en: That if he betroths: a woman after he abandoned his faith, his betrothal is a betrothal.

notes.he: ובעיא גט:
notes.en: His betrothal is a betrothal: and she requires a bill of divorce.

messages.text: In the case of one who comes to accept upon himself the commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status except for one matter, which he does not wish to observe, he is not accepted, and he is not trustworthy even with regard to those matters that he does wish to accept upon himself. Likewise, in the case of a gentile who comes to convert and takes upon himself to accept the words of Torah except for one matter, he is not accepted as a convert.

notes.he: מפרש בתוספתא במסכת דמאי שלא יתן תרומה ומעשר לעם הארץ ושלא יעשה טהרות אצל עם הארץ ושיאכל חולין בטהרה ושיעשר את שהוא אוכל ואת שהוא מוכר ואת שהוא לוקח:
notes.en: Matters of ḥaver status: the Tosefta in tractate Demai explains them: that he not give teruma or tithe to an am ha’aretz, that he not prepare his ritually pure food at an am ha’aretz’s, that he eat non-sacred food in purity, and that he tithe what he eats, what he sells and what he buys.

notes.dh: חוץ מדבר אחד אין מקבלין אותו
notes.he: דאמרינן הואיל ואין יכול לעמוד באותו דבר [ודאי לא יעמוד נמי באחרים]:
notes.en: Except for one matter, he is not accepted: for we say, since he cannot keep that one matter, [he will certainly not keep the others either].

messages.text: Even if he refuses to accept one detail of rabbinic law, he is not accepted.

notes.he: חומרא דרבנן:
notes.en: A detail of the scribes: a rabbinic stringency.

notes.he: אגר שבא לקבל עליו כל דברי תורה קאי ברייתא (ודאי לא יעמוד נמי באחרים):
notes.en: Even one detail: this part of the baraita refers to the gentile who comes to accept all the words of the Torah. [A bracketed gloss in the text repeats: he will certainly not keep the others either.]

messages.text: And similarly, in the case of a Levite who comes to accept the matters of a Levite, or a priest who comes to accept the matters of priesthood, except for one matter, he is not accepted.

notes.he: לשורר ולשרת ולהיות שוער:
notes.en: Matters of Levite status: to sing, to serve and to be a gatekeeper.

messages.text: As it is stated: “He among the sons of Aaron, that sacrifices the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, shall have the right thigh for a portion” (Leviticus 7:33). This means that with regard to the Temple service, which is handed over to the sons of Aaron, any priest who does not admit to it in its entirety has no share in the priesthood.

verse.he: הַמַּקְרִיב אֶת־דַּם הַשְּׁלָמִים וְאֶת־הַחֵלֶב מִבְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן לוֹ תִהְיֶה שׁוֹק הַיָּמִין לְמָנָה׃
verse.en: he from among Aaron’s sons who offers the blood and the fat of the offering of well-being shall get the right thigh as his portion.

notes.he: משמע שיהא נוהג כל דין בני אהרן לו תהיה שוק הימין למנה:
notes.en: Among the sons of Aaron: this implies that he must observe every law of the sons of Aaron, [and only then] “he shall have the right thigh for a portion.”

messages.text: In the case of one who comes to accept upon himself a commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status, if we have seen that he practices such matters in private, within his home, he is accepted, and afterward he is taught the precise details of being a ḥaver. But if we have not seen him act as a ḥaver in his home, he is taught first and afterward accepted.

notes.he: קודם שקיבל בפנינו היה נוהג עליו דין חבירות שאין לחושדו ולומר לפנים הוא עושה:
notes.en: That he practices in private: before he accepted it in our presence, he was already conducting himself by the law of ḥaver status, so there is no reason to suspect him and say he is doing it for show.

notes.he: שנחזיקנו כחבר וכנאמן לכל דבריו:
notes.en: He is accepted: we treat him as a ḥaver and as trustworthy in all his affairs.

notes.he: אם ראינוהו שנוהג בצנעא בתוך ביתו קודם לכך מקבלין אותו מיד ואח"כ מלמדין אותו:
notes.en: If we saw him practicing privately within his home before this, he is accepted at once, and afterward he is taught.

messages.text: Whether in this case or that case, he is first accepted, and he then continues to learn in the usual manner, i.e., as a ḥaver he learns from others how to behave.

An am ha’aretz who wishes to become a ḥaver is accepted first with regard to hands, i.e., he is presumed to be stringent concerning the ritual purity of his hands by making sure to wash his hands before handling pure items, and afterward he is accepted as trustworthy for purity in general.

notes.he: שיטול ידיו קודם אכילה וקודם שיגע באוכלין דתרומה דידים שניות הן:
notes.en: For hands [kenafayim]: that he wash his hands before eating and before touching foods of teruma, for hands are in second-degree impurity.

notes.he: לחומר שאר טהרות ונחזיק טהרותיו כטהרות גמורות לאכול תרומתו כתרומה טהורה:
notes.en: For ritually pure items: for the stringencies of the other matters of purity, so that we treat his pure foods as fully pure, and his teruma may be eaten as pure teruma.

notes.he: מקבלין לכנפים לנטילת ידים אם קיבל עליו להזהר שלא לאכול בלא נטילת ידים ובכל דבר שצריך לנטילת ידים:
notes.en: One is accepted for kenafayim, for washing the hands: if he accepted upon himself to be careful not to eat without washing his hands, and in everything that requires washing the hands.

notes.he: ליכל חולין בטהרה:
notes.en: Afterward he is accepted for ritually pure items: to eat non-sacred food in purity.

messages.text: And if he says: I wish to accept purity only with regard to hands, he is accepted for this. If he wishes to accept upon himself the stringencies of a ḥaver with regard to ritual purity but he does not accept upon himself the stringencies with regard to hands, i.e., to wash his hands, which is a simple act, he is not accepted even for purity in general.

notes.he: דאינו משייר דבר שלם שהרי מקבל עליו נטילת ידים וזהו עיקר אכילת חולין בטהרה:
notes.en: He is accepted: for he is not leaving out a whole matter, since he accepts the washing of hands, and that is the essence of eating non-sacred food in purity.

notes.he: דכיון דבדין נטילת ידים שדבר קל הוא לעשות אינו יכול לעמוד כל שכן בשאר:
notes.en: He has not accepted even for ritually pure items: for since he cannot keep the law of washing hands, which is an easy thing to do, all the more so the rest.

notes.he: כלומר שאין סומכין עליו אף לכמה שקיבל דאמרינן מדלא יכול לעמוד במה שצריך נטילת ידים כ"ש בשאר טהרות:
notes.en: He has not accepted even for ritually pure items: that is, we do not rely on him even for what he did accept, for we say: since he could not keep what requires washing the hands, all the more so the rest of purity.

messages.text: Until when is he accepted, i.e., how much time must elapse before he is considered trustworthy as a ḥaver? Beit Shammai say: With regard to liquids, thirty days. With regard to impurity of clothing, about which ḥaverim would be careful as well, twelve months. And Beit Hillel say: Both with regard to this, liquids, and that, clothing, he must maintain the practice for twelve months before he is fully accepted as a ḥaver.

notes.he: דברי חבירות שנקבלנו לאלתר ונחזיקנו בחבר:
notes.en: Until when is he accepted: for ḥaver status, so that we accept him at once and treat him as a ḥaver?

notes.he: שאם קיבל עליו דברי חבירות עד שלשים יום מהמנינן ליה מכאן ואילך בטהרות משקין שטומאתן קלה דטומאת משקין מדרבנן בפ' קמא דפסחים (דף טז:):
notes.en: For liquids, thirty days: if he took ḥaver status upon himself [and kept it] for thirty days, from then on we trust him with the purity of liquids, whose impurity is light, for the impurity of liquids is rabbinic, as in the first chapter of Pesaḥim (16b).

notes.he: להחזיק כסותו כחבר דאמר במסכת חגיגה (דף יח:) בגדי עם הארץ מדרס לפרושים:
notes.en: For clothing: to treat his clothing as a ḥaver’s, for it says in tractate Ḥagiga (18b): the garments of an am ha’aretz have the status of midras for Perushim.

notes.he: אם קיבל עליו דברי חבירות לשנים עשר חדש:
notes.en: Twelve months: if he took ḥaver status upon himself for twelve months.

notes.he: כלומר כמה חזינן ליה דאיזדהר בטהרה דמקבלין ליה בנאמן על הטהרות:
notes.en: Until when is he accepted: that is, how long must we see him being careful about purity for him to be accepted as trustworthy for ritually pure items?

notes.he: לטהרת משקין ל' יום:
notes.en: For liquids: for the purity of liquids, thirty days.

notes.he: לכסות לטהרת בגדים כדאמרינן בגדי עם הארץ מדרס לפרושים כו':
notes.en: For clothing: for the purity of garments, as we say: the garments of an am ha’aretz have the status of midras for Perushim, and so on.

messages.text: If so, this is one of the rare cases of the leniencies of Beit Shammai and of the stringencies of Beit Hillel, and yet it is not included in tractate Eduyyot, which lists all of the cases where Beit Shammai are more lenient than Beit Hillel.
messages.quote: And Beit Hillel say: Both with regard to this and that, for twelve months

notes.dh: הוה ליה מקולי בית שמאי ומחומרי בית הלל
notes.he: וליתנייה גבי קולי בית שמאי וחומרי בית הלל במסכת עדיות (פ"ה מ"א) דאמרינן ששה דברים מקולי בית שמאי ומחומרי בית הילל ואם איתא ליתני הא. ל"א עד כמה מקבלין אותו דאמרן לעיל אם נהג מתחלה בצינעא בתוך ביתו מקבלין אותו מיד ועד כמה ינהג מתחלה שנקבלנו מיד:
notes.en: This would be among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel: and it should be taught along with the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel in tractate Eduyyot (5:1), where we say six matters are among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel. If this were so, this too should be taught there. Another version: “until when is he accepted” refers to what we said above, that if he first practiced privately within his home he is accepted at once; [the question is] how long he must first practice so that we accept him at once.

messages.text: Rather, the text of the baraita must be emended so that it reads: Beit Hillel say: Both with regard to this, liquids and that, clothing, he must maintain the practice for thirty days before he is fully accepted as a ḥaver.
A mnemonic to remember the topics from here until the end of the chapter: Ḥaver; student; sky-blue dye [tekhelet]; tax; return; tax collector; by himself.

One who comes to accept upon himself a commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status must accept it in the presence of three ḥaverim. But his children and the members of his household are not required to accept the status of ḥaver separately in the presence of three ḥaverim.

Even his children and the members of his household must accept the status of ḥaver in the presence of three ḥaverim, because a ḥaver, who accepted it himself in the presence of three others, is not comparable to the son of a ḥaver, who accepted that status only due to his father but did not accept it himself explicitly, and their accepting the status not in the presence of three people is insufficient.

notes.he: הוא עצמו לבן חבר מחמת קבלת אביו שאין לו שום קבלה אלא סרך אביו דודאי אביו מיזדהר טפי. ל"א האי לפי שאינו דומה תנא קמא קאמר ליה מה טעם בניו ובני ביתו אין צריכין לקבל לפי שאינו דומה חבר שקיבל לבן חבר שקיבל אביו דבן חבר לא חשיד. ובתוספתא גרסינן שאין דומה חבר שקלקל לבן חבר שקלקל במסכת דמאי:
notes.en: Because a ḥaver who accepted is not comparable: [a ḥaver who accepted it] himself is not comparable to the son of a ḥaver [who has it] through his father’s acceptance, for he has no acceptance of his own, only his father’s habit, and his father is certainly more careful. Another version: this “because it is not comparable” is the first tanna speaking to him: why do his children and household not need to accept? Because a ḥaver who accepted is not comparable to the son of a ḥaver whose father accepted, for the son of a ḥaver is not suspect. And in the Tosefta, tractate Demai, we read: for a ḥaver who went astray is not comparable to the son of a ḥaver who went astray.

notes.he: לפי שאינו דומה חבר שקיבל ט"א אינו דומה חבר שקיבל וכן שקיבל הכי משמע כיון דאמרת דחבר עצמו צריך לקבל בפני ג' כ"ש בן חבר שצריך לקבל בפני ג' מש"ה הת"ק קאי דאמרינן בניו ובני ביתו אינו צריך לקבל אע"ג דאיהו גופיה צריך לקבל בפני ג' אינו דומה חבר בן עם הארץ לבן חבר. דחבר בן עם הארץ לא למד בבית אביו וצריך לו לקבל בפני ג' אבל בן חבר דסריך בטהרות שנוהג בבית אביו אין צריך לקבל בפני ג':
notes.en: Because a ḥaver who accepted is not comparable [a printed note: it seems it should read “a ḥaver who accepted to the son of a ḥaver who accepted”]: this implies, and so on, that he must accept before three. Another version: “it is not comparable,” and so on, refers to the first tanna, which is why he said that his children and household, and so on. Another version: “a ḥaver who accepted is not comparable,” and likewise “who accepted,” means this: since you said that a ḥaver himself must accept before three, all the more so the son of a ḥaver must accept before three. Hence the first tanna, who says his children and household need not accept: although the ḥaver himself must accept before three, a ḥaver who is the son of an am ha’aretz is not comparable to the son of a ḥaver. For a ḥaver who is the son of an am ha’aretz did not learn it in his father’s house, and he must accept before three; but the son of a ḥaver, who is used to purity because it is practiced in his father’s house, need not accept before three.

messages.text: One who comes to accept upon himself a commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status must accept it in the presence of three ḥaverim, and even a Torah scholar who wishes to become a ḥaver must accept the status of ḥaver in the presence of three ḥaverim.

But an elder who sits and studies Torah in a yeshiva is not required to accept the status of ḥaver in the presence of three ḥaverim, as he already accepted it upon himself from the moment he sat and dedicated himself to study Torah in yeshiva.

Even a Torah scholar is not required to accept the status of ḥaver in the presence of three ḥaverim; and not only does he have the status of ḥaver without an explicit declaration in the presence of three ḥaverim, but others can accept that they wish to become a ḥaver in his presence.
This mishna, i.e., the ruling that a Torah scholar must declare his intent to become a ḥaver in the presence of three ḥaverim, was taught in the days of the son of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus.
messages.quote: and even a Torah scholar must accept the status of ḥaver in the presence of three ḥaverim

notes.he: דאפי' תלמיד חכם צריך לקבל:
notes.en: This mishna was taught: that even a Torah scholar must accept.

notes.dh: בימי בנו של ר' חנינא נשנית משנה זו
notes.he: דת"ח צריך לקבל בפני ג' דאיהו הוה חשיד אפי' ת"ח בטהרותיו אא"כ קבלו בפני ג':
notes.en: This mishna was taught in the days of the son of Rabbi Ḥanina: that a Torah scholar must accept before three, for he would suspect even a Torah scholar regarding his ritually pure items unless they had accepted before three.

messages.text: At that time, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei were uncertain about a certain matter of ritual purity. The Sages sent a delegation of their students to the son of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus and told them to go and tell him to examine this matter.

notes.he: בסדר טהרות לא גרסי'. בטהרות עצמן אירע להן מעשה ונסתפקה הלכה:
notes.en: Concerning ritually pure items: we do not read “in the order of Teharot”; rather, an incident happened to them with ritually pure items themselves, and the halakha was in doubt.

notes.he: שדרו זוג דרבנן:
notes.en: The Sages sent: they sent a pair of Sages.

messages.text: The students found him while he was carrying items that were ritually pure. The son of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus seated Sages from his own yeshiva next to the students who came to ask the question, because he did not trust these students to keep his items pure. And he stood and examined the matter.

notes.he: מתלמידיו שקיבלו עליהן דברי חבירות אותיב בהדי הנך שלוחים וקאי איהו לעיוני בשאילתם:
notes.en: He seated Sages of his own: some of his students who had accepted ḥaver status upon themselves; he seated them beside those messengers, and he himself stood to examine their question.

notes.he: מתלמידיו לשמור טהרותיו עד שהלך לעיין בדבר:
notes.en: He seated Sages of his own: some of his students, to guard his ritually pure items while he went to examine the matter.

messages.text: The students returned and came and told Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei that the son of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus had treated them as though they had the status of amei ha’aretz.

This one’s father, i.e., Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus, degraded Torah scholars by not trusting them with matters of ritual purity. And he too, the son of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus, degrades Torah scholars.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehuda said to them in anger:

notes.he: אגב ריתחיה קאמר ולא היא:
notes.en: This one’s father, and so on: he said this in his anger, and it is not so.

notes.dh: אביו של זה ביזה תלמידים שלנו
notes.he: על הטהרות כמו שעשה בנו:
notes.en: This one’s father degraded our students [so Tosafot’s text; the daf reads “Torah scholars”]: regarding ritually pure items, as his son did.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehuda Let the honor of the elder, i.e., both the father and son, be left in its place. He did not act in this manner to degrade Torah scholars. Rather, from the day the Temple was destroyed, the priests were accustomed to act with a higher standard for themselves, and they decided that they will not pass ritually pure items to any other person. Therefore, the son of Rabbi Ḥanina, as a priest, acted appropriately.

notes.he: האב והבן:
notes.en: The honor of the elder: the father and the son.

notes.he: מעלה. ר' חנינא בן אנטיגנוס כהן היה:
notes.en: Silsul: a higher standard. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus was a priest.

notes.he: לר' יהודה היאך נהג בהם שלא רצה להאמין להם טהרותיו. א"ל ר' יוסי לר' יהודה כבוד זקן יהא מונח במקומו כלומר אל תחשדיה במבזה ת"ח:
notes.en: They told him: [the students told] Rabbi Yehuda how he had treated them, that he did not want to trust them with his ritually pure items. Rabbi Yosei said to Rabbi Yehuda: Let the honor of the elder be left in its place; that is, do not suspect him of degrading Torah scholars.

notes.he: אלא מיום שחרב בהמ"ק נהגו חכמים סילסול חומרא:
notes.en: Rather, from the day the Temple was destroyed, the Sages [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads “priests”] adopted silsul, a stringency.

messages.text: In the case of a ḥaver that died, his wife and children and members of his household retain their presumptive status until they are suspected of engaging in inappropriate deeds. And similarly, in the case of a courtyard in which one sells sky-blue dye, it retains its presumptive status as a place in which fit sky-blue dye is sold until it is disqualified due to the merchant’s unscrupulous behavior.

notes.he: שימכרו בה קלא אילן לשם תכלת:
notes.en: In its presumptive status until it is disqualified: until they sell indigo dye [kela ilan] there as tekhelet.

messages.text: The former wife of an am ha’aretz who later marries a ḥaver, and likewise the daughter of an am ha’aretz who marries a ḥaver, and likewise the slave of an am ha’aretz who is sold to a ḥaver, must all accept upon themselves a commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status.

notes.dh: צריכין לקבל דברי חבירות בתחלה גרסי' ולא גרסי' כבתחלה
notes.he: ובתוספתא גרסינן הכי בבתחלה כלומר מתחלה קודם שנחזיקנו בחבירות ואע"ג דאמרן לעיל בניו ובני ביתו אין צריכין לקבל הכא שאני הואיל ובשעת קבלה לא הוו גביה ואיכא למימר דסרכייהו קמא נקטי:
notes.en: They must accept ḥaver status “battehilla”: so we read, and we do not read “kebattehilla” [as at first]. And in the Tosefta we read “battehilla,” that is, at the outset, before we treat them as ḥaverim. And although we said above that his children and household need not accept, here it is different, since at the time of the acceptance they were not with him, and one could say they keep to their former habits.

messages.text: But with regard to the former wife of a ḥaver who later marries an am ha’aretz, and likewise the daughter of a ḥaver who marries an am ha’aretz, and likewise the slave of a ḥaver who was sold to an am ha’aretz, these people need not accept upon themselves a commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status ab initio, as each of them is already accustomed to behave as a ḥaver.

notes.he: אם חזרו תחת יד חבר:
notes.en: They need not accept: if they come back under the authority of a ḥaver.

messages.text: They too must accept upon themselves a commitment to observe the matters associated with ḥaver status ab initio.

There was an incident involving a certain woman who married a ḥaver and would tie [koma’at] for him phylacteries on his hand, and she later married a tax collector and would tie for him tax seals on his hand, which shows that her new husband had a great influence on her level of piety.
messages.lead: And similarly, Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would illustrate this point and say in the name of Rabbi Meir:

notes.he: קושרת:
notes.en: Koma’at: ties.

notes.he: שיש חותמות למוכסים וכשנותנין להן המכס הם נותנין לו חותם כדי שלא יתבענו מוכס שני:
notes.en: Tax seals: tax collectors have seals, and when people pay them the tax they give the payer a seal so that a second tax collector will not demand it from him again.

messages.text: The baraitot on ḥaver status continue on 31a, with those who accepted it and then retracted.
